assets.usage: Reference or inset showing a labeled modern cast of the inscription, with an explicit caption that the photograph depicts a cast in Milan, not the archaeological stone at Caesarea.
assets.anachronismsAndLimits: Do not present as an object currently located at Caesarea or as a photograph of the original. This image is not an ancient image; the cast reproduces a first-century inscription.

assets.author: Chmee2

assets.usage: Regional landmark / present-day site reference only; not a scene-specific artifact for Pilate's prefecture.
assets.anachronismsAndLimits: Aqueduct phases are not dated on this file page and the visible structure should not be assumed to have existed in precisely this form in 27–36 CE. Avoid as a close period reconstruction.

assets.author: Carole Raddato (Flickr account Following Hadrian)
assets.usage: Possible modern-site reference for the monumental Roman city, provided image label states that the visible Marble Court is a modern archaeological reconstruction.
assets.anachronismsAndLimits: Not a view of the city in 170–180 CE: the visible court was substantially reassembled in the twentieth century, and the complex is dated slightly later than the Melito episode. Do not imply it is a documented Christian meeting place or synagogue.

assets.author: Dosseman
assets.usage: Useful only for later Jewish communal continuity in Sardis, if relevant to a later episode; unsuitable for a 170–180 CE Melito episode without strong date caveat.
assets.anachronismsAndLimits: Building dates are the Commons description, not a directly inspected excavation report. The page says substantial restoration makes original and restored fabric difficult to distinguish. Later than Melito's proposed lifetime/event.

assets.author: Zde
assets.usage: Best of these candidates as a Roman-period city landmark near Paul's conventional Corinthian stay around 50–52 CE, with attribution and an explicit archaeological-site caption.
assets.anachronismsAndLimits: Dedication to Octavia is not secure; Temple E is a conventional alias and the identification/dedication is debated. It is not evidence of Paul's presence at the temple or of a Christian assembly there.

assets.author: MM
assets.license: Public domain, released by the photographer without conditions to the extent permitted by law.
assets.usage: Present-day landmark and geographic reference. Archaic construction does not imply absence from Roman Corinth; do not treat the surviving fabric as a complete first-century reconstruction.
assets.anachronismsAndLimits: The temple predated Paul but remained in Roman Corinth with modifications. This 2006 photograph cannot establish the precise first-century layout or which alterations were already present.
